stances.claim: The conviction is not oxymoronic: an honest official can be convicted by an honest judge when the law is applied to the facts as found -- Padaca's honesty as a public servant does not exempt her from criminal liability for negligently permitting the misappropriation of P18 million in public funds.
stances.rhetorical_move: oxymoron-resolution thesis (the apparent contradiction is the column's setup)

stances.claim: Padaca had no authority to sign the MOA on Jan 8, 2006; the subsequent Jan 31, 2006 PB resolution authorized her prospectively but conditioned the MOA on PB 'review and ratification,' which she did not seek before the Feb 23, 2006 release of P25 million; malversation was consummated at that release, and the eventual Jan 31, 2007 ratification cannot retroactively cure criminal liability per Art. 89 RPC.
stances.rhetorical_move: chronological-criminal-liability analysis (the dates tell the story)

stances.claim: The separate conviction under Anti-Graft Law Section 3(e) is permitted because that provision punishes 'undue injury' 'in addition to acts or omissions already penalized by existing law' -- meaning the same P18M unaccounted balance can ground BOTH malversation under the Penal Code AND a Section 3(e) Anti-Graft conviction.
stances.rhetorical_move: double-statute-application explanation (the same facts, two laws)

stances.claim: Padaca's reliance on Lamonera's legal opinion was improper because Lamonera was a registered incorporator of the Foundation -- a textbook conflict of interest that should have disqualified his opinion from being a defense.
stances.rhetorical_move: conflict-of-interest disqualification of an internal legal opinion

stances.claim: It is critical for public understanding to distinguish: Padaca was neither charged with nor convicted of stealing public money -- the charge was negligence-permitted malversation BY OTHERS plus the resulting undue injury to the Province.
CJ withholds further legal commentary on criminal liability pending the MR, since Padaca has publicly announced she will file one; this withholding is methodological respect for pending proceedings.

notable_anecdotes: The opening 'An oxymoronic title, this column appears to have. But that is the situation in People v. Padaca' -- CJ's signature move of building the column around an apparent contradiction that the body resolves.

The chronological table of fault: MOA signed Jan 8, 2006 (no authority) → PB authorizes Jan 31, 2006 (after the fact) → P25M released Feb 23, 2006 (malversation consummated) → ratification Jan 31, 2007 (one year too late; cannot cure criminal liability per Art. 89 RPC).

Lamonera's conflict-of-interest -- Provincial Legal Officer who is also a 'registered incorporator' of the very Foundation receiving the P25 million -- surfaced as the structural defect in Padaca's defense.
'Justices Fernandez and Moreno are no pushovers either' -- CJ's quiet validation that the conviction is not a single-justice idiosyncrasy.

The careful framing 'Padaca was neither charged with nor convicted of stealing the people's money. Rather, the SBN found her guilty of allowing others, through her negligence, to malverse public funds' -- CJ's most precise rendering of negligence-permitted malversation as a distinct offense from theft.
Closing tribute to both parties -- 'whether the reputedly honest public servant can convince the equally honest judge' -- symmetric praise for both Padaca and Cabotaje-Tang.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with an apparent oxymoron -- 'Honest official convicted by honest judge' -- and spends the column resolving it. Grace Padaca, the Isabela governor (2004-2010), former broadcast journalist, 'Symbol of People Power' and 2008 Ramon Magsaysay Award for Public Service laureate, was convicted by the Sandiganbayan on Nov 15, 2019 of malversation under the Revised Penal Code and of violating Section 3(e) of the Anti-Graft Law (RA 3019). The 57-page ponencia by Presiding Justice Amparo M. Cabotaje-Tang (joined unanimously by Justices Bernelito R. Fernandez and Ronald B. Moreno -- 'who are no pushovers either') traces the chronology: Padaca signed the MOA with the Economic Development for Western Isabela and Northern Luzon Foundation Inc. on Jan 8, 2006 without authority. The Provincial Board's Jan 31, 2006 resolution authorized her prospectively but conditioned the MOA on PB review and ratification -- which she did not seek before the Feb 23, 2006 release of P25 million, of which only P7 million was returned, leaving P18 million unaccounted. By the time the PB ratified the MOA on Jan 31, 2007, malversation had already been consummated; Art. 89 of the Revised Penal Code excludes ratification as a ground for extinguishment of criminal liability. The Anti-Graft Law Section 3(e) conviction stands separately because that provision punishes undue injury 'in addition to acts or omissions... already penalized by existing law' -- and Padaca improperly relied on the legal opinion of Provincial Legal Officer Johnas Lamonera, who was ethically conflicted as a 'registered incorporator' of the Foundation. CJ is careful to clarify: Padaca was neither charged with nor convicted of stealing public money; the SBN found her guilty of allowing others, through her negligence, to malverse public funds. He defers further commentary pending her announced MR -- and closes with symmetric tribute: will the reputedly honest public servant be able to convince the equally honest judge to change her mind on reconsideration?
